title: Operational slab credit handoff and HC speed probe
description: Compact scenario sheet to test a credit-handoff mechanism between product feature teams and central ops, measure how quickly HC can be re-phased in response to pricing deltas, and surface glide-paths for short-cycle hiring tied to slab credits.
executive_summary: We prototyped a three-slab credit handoff and a fast-hire corridor to see how pricing moves (±10–40%) would change hiring speed and runway. Primary output: a recommended operating rule that ties 1) credit pool utilization, 2) token price band, and 3) a 12-week headcount speed ladder. Early result: with a conservative 25% price compression, we can delay 18 FTEs over 4 quarters without breaching SLA buffer if burst credits are staged and feature pacing enforced.
assumptions: Base token price (current average): $0.0035 per token
Credit pool convertible to 75% effective capacity (leakage/inefficiencies included)
SLA buffer target: 99.9% availability with 20% spare capacity for spikes

sensitivity_analysis_notes: Cost deltas are back-of-envelope using token price * tokens/mo. Headcount impacts use ratio of cost delta to fully-burdened FTE annualized. This sheet models converting credit pool into FTE months (credit-runway conversion factor = 0.75). We account for a 10% efficiency loss in fast hires and 20% conversion slippage for contractor conversions.
operational_slab_credit_model:
Credit pool (Q-start): $9.6M (cash-backed credits)
Slab bands:
 - Green slab: immediate burst (0–30% utilization): usable for latency spikes, cost-insensitive; reserve 40% of pool
 - Yellow slab: sustained burst (30–70%): tied to feature pacing and gating workflow; reserve 40% of pool
 - Red slab: emergency drawdown (70–100%): requires Exec approval + product pacing
Handoff rule: product team requests yellow slab; finance validates via automated scoreboard showing tokens burned per feature in last 28 days. Ops injects capacity and credits in 48 hours if scoreboard passes.
triggers_and_action_matrix: Trigger: 2-week token burn > 120% rolling baseline -> Action: open yellow slab, defer non-critical hires by 25%
Trigger: observed 3% day-over-day price compression for 10 days -> Action: freeze fast-lane hires, run contractor surge model
Trigger: credit pool utilization > 55% -> Action: require feature-level approval and ramp down non-essential routes by 20%
Trigger: customer SLA miss > incident threshold -> Action: immediate red slab review, engage execs and customer-success for elevated credits
fast_hire_corridor: 12-week ladder: Week 0–4: sourcing + onboarding (contractor-first), Week 5–8: productivity ramp (50–70%), Week 9–12: convert to FTE if retention and quality metrics met. Cost amortization: assume 1.15x recruitment premium for fast hires. If pricing compression >25%, corridor elongates to 20 weeks and conversion rate drops to 35%.
recommended_playbook: 1) Adopt a 3-slab credit pool with automated scoreboard gating. 2) Tie 60% of non-critical feature releases to yellow-slab approval to smooth token demand. 3) Maintain a 12-week fast-hire corridor funded from credits for high-priority infra/SRE hires. 4) In worst-case (-40%), default to contractor surge + quantization rollouts and preserve SLA via model fallbacks.
